1707.d: To enfold, entangle; pass: To be involved in. From en and pleko; to entwine, i.e. involve with.

1044.d: Gangrene, mortification. From graino; an ulcer.

1744.d: To clothe; mid: I enter, creep into. From ennomos and duno; to sink (compare enduo) on, i.e. (figuratively) sneak.

1133.d: A woman, with all a woman's weakness, a poor weak woman, a silly woman. A diminutive from gune; a little woman.

1552.d: Perfectly evident, manifest. From ek and delos; wholly evident.

1114.d: A conjuror, juggler, sorcerer; a tricky (crafty) deceiver, imposter. From goao; properly, a wizard, i.e. an imposter.

1650.d: A proof, possibly: a persuasion; reproof. From elegcho; proof, conviction.

1882.d: A straightening up again, i.e. rectification.

1930.d: To straighten further, i.e. arrange additionally.

1468.d: Self-controlled. From en and kratos; strong in a thing, i.e. self-controlled.

1993.d: To muzzle, silence, stop the mouth. From epi and stoma; to put something over the mouth, i.e. to silence.

1612.d: To change for the worse, corrupt, pervert. From ek and strepho; to pervert.

1595.d: Willing, with right good will, voluntary, spontaneous. Neuter of a derivative from hekon; voluntariness.

1667.d: To roll, roll up, fold up. A form of heilisso; to coil or wrap.

1366.d: (lit: twain-mouthed; hence: of a sword, as a drinker of blood), two-edged. From dis and stoma; double-edged.

1338.d: To pass through (to), come through (to), pierce. From dia and the base of hikanos; to reach through, i.e. Penetrate.

1421.d: Difficult to interpret, hard to be understood. From dus- and a presumed derivative of hermeneuo; difficult of explanation.

1838.d: Condition, state, habit, use, especially: good condition of body or soul. From echo; habit, i.e. practice.

1008.d: Fodder, food, herbage. From bosko; herbage.

1090.d: To work the soil, cultivate the earth. From georgos; to till.

1181.d: A tenth part, a tithe. Feminine of dekatos; a tenth, i.e. As a percentage or tithe.

1336.d: Neuter of a compound of dia and a derivative of an alternate of phero; carried through, i.e. perpetually.

1075.d: To put into a genealogy, reckon my descent. From genea and logos; to reckon by generations, i.e. Trace in genealogy.
r: who did not trace his descent

1183.d: To tithe, collect tithe from. From dekate; to tithe, i.e. To give or take a tenth.

1898.d: Bringing in (besides or in addition), introduction, importation. From a compound of epi and eisago; a superintroduction.

1450.d: A surety, security. From en and guion; pledged, i.e. A bondsman.

1151.d: A heifer, young cow. Probably from the base of damazo; a heifer.

1457.d: To consecrate, dedicate, renovate. From egkainia; to renew, i.e. Inaugurate.

1596.d: Willingly, of one's own accord, spontaneously. Adverb from the same as hekousion; voluntarily.

1561.d: A waiting for, expectation. From ekdechomai; expectation.

1796.d: To insult, outrage, treat contemptuously, mock at. From en and hubrizo; to insult.

1217.d: An artisan, builder, maker; one who labors for the public. From demos and ergon; a worker for the people, i.e. Mechanic.

1297.d: A mandate, decree, edict. From diatasso; an arrangement, i.e. edict.

1952.d: To fail, fall short. From epi and leipo; to leave upon, i.e. to be insufficient for.

1066.d: Gideon, one of the Judges of Israel. Of Hebrew origin; Gedeonon), an Israelite.

1701.d: Mockery, scoffing, scorn. From empaizo; derision.

1192.d: The skin or hide of an animal. From dero; a hide.

1585.d: To forget entirely, make to forget. Middle voice from ek and lanthano; to be utterly oblivious of.

1516.d: Peaceable, disposed to peace, profitable. From eirene; pacific; by implication, salutary.

1983.d: To exercise oversight, care for, visit. From epi and skopeo; to oversee; by implication, to beware.

1105.d: Darkness, gloom; a thick cloud. Akin to nephos; gloom.

1383.d: A test, trial, what is genuine. Neuter of a presumed derivative of dokime; a testing; by implication, trustworthiness.

1503.d: To be like, resemble. Apparently a primary verb; to resemble.

1374.d: (lit: of two souls, of two selves), double-minded, wavering. From dis and psuche; two-spirited, i.e. Vacillating.

1828.d: To drag forth, i.e. to entice.

1185.d: To allure, entice (by a bait). From the base of dolos; to entrap, i.e. delude.

1721.d: Inborn, ingrown, congenital, natural, rooted, implanted. From en and a derivative of phuo; implanted.

1953.d: Forgetfulness, oblivion. From a derivative of epilanthanomai; negligence.

1724.d: Marine, living in the sea. From en and hals; in the sea, i.e. Marine.

1032.d: To cause to gush forth, send forth. A primary verb; to swell out, i.e. to gush.

1990.d: Skillful, experienced, knowing. From epistamai; intelligent.

1141.d: Demon-like, such as demons have. From daimonion and daimon; d?Mon-like.

1710.d: To travel in, i.e. to trade.

1830.d: To search diligently, I examine carefully (minutely). From ek and ereunao; to explore.

1804.d: To announce publicly, proclaim. From ek and the base of aggelos; to publish, i.e. Celebrate.

1942.d: A covering, cloak, veil, pretext. From epikalupto; a covering, i.e. pretext.

1708.d: A plaiting, braiding. From empleko; elaborate braiding of the hair.

1745.d: A putting on of clothing. From enduo; investment with clothing.

1134.d: Belonging to woman, of woman, female. From gune; feminine.

1906.d: Inquiry, request, appeal, demand; a profession, pledge. From eperotao; an inquiry.

1954.d: Remaining, that is left over, still left. From epi and loipoy; left over, i.e. Remaining.

1618.d: Intent, constant, strenuous, intense; met: earnest, zealous. From ekteino; intent.

1463.d: To clothe oneself (originally: To tie round in a knot).

1957.d: To testify earnestly, bear witness to. From epi and martureo; to attest further, i.e. Corroborate.

1862.d: A promise. From epaggello; a self-committal.

1539.d: At every time, always. As if from hekastos and tote; at every time.

1811.d: To follow after, imitate. From ek and akoloutheo; to follow out, i.e. to imitate, obey, yield to.

1306.d: To shine through, dawn (of the light coming through the shadows). From dia and augazo; to glimmer through, i.e. Break.

1955.d: Solution, explanation, interpretation; release. From epiluo; explanation, i.e. Application.

1597.d: Long ago, for a long while.

1460.d: To dwell in, among. From en and katoikeo; to settle down in a place, i.e. Reside.

1792.d: To revel (in), live luxuriously, riot. From en and truphao; to revel in.

1007.d: Bosor, father of Balaam. Of Hebrew origin; Bosor, a Moabite.

1649.d: Rebuke, reproof, refutation. From elegcho; refutation, i.e. Reproof.

1829.d: Vomit. From a comparative of ek and a presumed erao; vomit, i.e. Food disgorged.

1004.d: Mud, mire, filth. Of uncertain derivation; mud.

1703.d: A mocker, scoffer. From empaizo; a derider, i.e. a false teacher.

1022.d: Tardiness, slowness, delay. From bradus; tardiness.

1425.d: Hard to understand. From dus- and a derivative of noieo; difficult of perception.

1361.d: Diotrephes. From the alternate of Zeus and trepho; Jove-nourished; Diotrephes, an opponent of Christianity.

1926.d: To accept, admit, welcome. From epi and dechomai; to admit (figuratively) teacher.

1864.d: To contend earnestly for. From epi and agonizomai; to struggle for.

1608.d: To be guilty of fornication. From ek and porneuo; to be utterly unchaste.

1164.d: An example, type; a thing shown. From the base of deiknuo; a specimen.

1890.d: To foam upon, i.e. to exhibit.

1113.d: A murmurer, grumbler. From gogguzo; a grumbler.

1692.d: To vomit forth. Of uncertain affinity; to vomit.

1472.d: To rub in, anoint. From en and chrio; to rub in, i.e. Besmear.

1045.d: Gad, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. Of Hebrew origin; Gad, a tribe of Israelites.

1673.d: Greek, the Greek language. From Hellen; Hellenic, i.e. Grecian.

1404.d: A dragon or huge serpent; met: Satan. Probably from an alternate form of derkomai; a fabulous kind of serpent.

1238.d: A head-wreath, crown, diadem. From a compound of dia and deo; a |diadem|.

1812.d: Six hundred. Plural ordinal from hex and hekaton; six hundred.

1009.d: A cluster (bunch) of grapes. Of uncertain derivation; a bunch.

1363.d: To double, render back double. From diplous; to render two-fold.

1661.d: Made of ivory, subst: ivory. From elephas; elephantine, i.e. composed of ivory.

1136.d: Gog, a symbolic name for some future Antichrist.
